ORC-1.subject: instruction-change acceptability and any verdict without a higher-rung oracle
ORC-1.mechanism: principal review at the PR checkpoint; spec consensus with exported decisions where one exists

ORC-3.subject: every commit's shape: the [ORACLE] section, the Oracle trailer, and the Token diff line on steering-text commits
ORC-3.mechanism: plugins/harness/hooks/commit-shape-gate.sh via PostToolUse on Bash; tested by tests/commit-shape-gate-test.sh

ORC-5.subject: the Token diff figure recorded on a steering-text commit
ORC-5.mechanism: re-run plugins/harness/skills/commit-protocol/scripts/token_diff.py --base <sha>^ --target <sha>; the file set derives from the commit's diff and the count_tokens endpoint is the reference

ORC-8.subject: each commit of a finished PR stack at merge time: its problem predates the branch (state, survives the merge) vs was created by the branch's own commits (journey, folded by the merger)
ORC-8.mechanism: the /merge skill runs skills/merge/scripts/classify_stack.py; claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 judges each commit's message plus the ordered sibling listing against skills/merge/rubric.md; leftover fixup!/squash!/amend! subjects are folds without a model call; the merger folds on fold verdicts, may overrule (it, not the model, is the merger), and re-runs the judge on the folded stack to verify a clean landing; nothing blocks a live implementer session — the implementer's branch is a licensed scratchpad; calibration corpus and held-out error rates live in evals/stack-provenance (labels derived from the principal's recorded fold actions in mono-repo PR history)

ORC-9.subject: the reviewer subagent's initial reasoning allocation: >=16,000 reasoning tokens before its first tool call
ORC-9.mechanism: the run's first generation in the session trace: the observability proxy labels a zero-reasoning turn 'response (NO REASONING)' (WARNING) and records per-turn output tokens; equivalently, thinking-before-first-tool extracted from the subagent transcript JSONL; checked on demand, not hook-enforced

ORC-10.subject: the stripped-sdk-runner kit's transport claims: authored requests — single-turn, tool-forced, and multi-turn tool transcripts over the streaming transport — keep claude -p's per-model-family wire shape minus the <system-reminder> contamination, the cache/structured-output/tools options track the CLI's feature-dependent wire, wire_capture relays byte-for-byte untouched, the think scheme's forced rounds land in the tool with 0 thinking tokens billed, and the dry-run scheme captures reasoning and first intended action with no working round ever sent
ORC-10.mechanism: plugins/harness/skills/skill-creator/stripped-sdk-runner/integration_test.py, live, self-contained, fixture-free, run once per model family (INTEGRATION_MODEL): mints a fresh claude -p capture through two chained wire_capture instances as the shape reference, runs four authored rollouts (cache-on CC shape, default, structured output, forced tools) plus a streamed tool-loop continuation through the same chain, and asserts relay byte-fidelity (inner vs outer sha256), shape parity of the cache-on wire via its shape_diff (only caller texts, the deliberately absent reminder, session ids, lengths, and the billing hash suffix may differ), the option contracts (default wire free of cache_control and feature betas; output_format wire carrying the schema, its beta, and a conforming JSON reply), clean-wire assertions on every authored capture, the reasoning invariant (substantial billed thinking must arrive as a streamed summary — the authored thinking.display=summarized unmask is the one deliberate wire addition, since the CLI omits the field and the server then suppresses the billed summary), and the tripwire — the -p reference smuggles a reminder, no authored wire does; on drift it prints the fresh wire values to re-freeze bare_runner's per-family WIRE profiles from; the tool-loop leg mints a second -p run that EXECUTES a Read call, so its follow-up request is the CLI's own tool_use/tool_result vocabulary, and the authored transcript replayed over stream_round (forced continuation) must keep that vocabulary and the -p header sequence, Accept-Encoding identity being the declared streaming exception; offline_test.py is the canned no-network no-login tier for parse/halt/refusal/quota/transcript/CLI mechanics and for the dry run's round-1-only, probe-halt, abort-rail, and default-roster contract (the captured envs/claude-code-* environment - system prompt and tool roster - on the wire verbatim when system/tools are omitted); the think scheme is verified live on opus-5 — verdict ok, 0 thinking tokens billed, typed answer matching locally computed ground truth

ORC-14.subject: whether a user-facing text meets the writing register the principal accepts: the writing-guard skill's directives WG-1..WG-5, covering final messages, questions to the user, commit messages, PR descriptions and artifact prose
ORC-14.mechanism: score the text against WG-1..WG-5 and against the 50 answered labels the principal gave over two labeling rounds (mono-repo scratch/2026-08-21-writing-guard/curation/round1-labels.json and curation/round2/round2-labels.json, analysis in sweep/ROUND2-ANALYSIS.md); the verdict aggregates over samples and carries a nonzero error rate, so no single text confirms or refutes a directive; the accepted floor is one repeat-confirmed 'okay' (r1-27 = r2-03) and one 'good' the principal qualified as 'closest to good' (r2-11), too thin for a numeric threshold; round 3 tests whether WG-5 ports to the commit genre and whether WG-4 holds in body position
